title: I'm working on a side-scrolling action shooter, and getting it to feel fluid is genuinely a challenge.
author: Dependent-Video7534
selftext:
I'm currently working on a side-scrolling run-and-gun in the vein of Metal Slug. So far I've got the core animation set done for two characters:

idle, run, shoot, melee, reload

One thing I ran into along the way: getting AI to generate sprite sheets that actually animate smoothly is genuinely hard. But seeing the characters finally move is still really satisfying, so I wanted to share where I'm at.

For code I'm mainly using Claude Code with Godot; art is Gemini + GPT-5.6.

Hoping I'll get the chance to finish this properly and release on Steam someday.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: Consider certain animation locks. They're quite smooth. But when you get hit and turn, the character starts falling back the other direction instead of the one they were actually hit in. Additionally allowing movement while legs are locked... Might want to separate leg animations from upper body if you're doing that so the character isn't sliding while reloading.

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body:
Your animation is pretty good.  There are a few animation frames that set backwards of slight off so you get an odd jump. You might see if you can get it to make an editor and you can scrub through the frames one by one so you can see this. 

Which sprite maker did you use for this? for wonders? for the animation lol

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for the feedback! You're right, there's definitely still a lot to adjust and plenty of work left to do.

For the animations, I used Ludo for the idle and run cycles.

comments.author: DamienNF
comments.body: the animarions look really not bad for AI generated. Are pixel graphics your deliberate choice? Because I'm using the same perspective for my game but use different approach for animations - generate 1 image with AI then prepare it in photoshop, then use Spine app to rig it and create animations

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body:
Thanks! I just genuinely like pixel-art games — there's a retro feel to them, so it's purely a personal preference. Good to hear your game is going for a similar look.

Speaking of Spine, that's a great approach too. I actually tried getting Claude Code to build skeletal animations via Blender + MCP, but it didn't work out that well. Impressive that you're able to make it work for your game, maybe I'll revisit skeletal animation and give Spine a try down the line.

Best of luck with your game too!

replies.author: DamienNF
replies.body: Actually splitting image to pieces, rigging and animations =  this is the only part of the game I'm doing manually with my hands - because for now I don't know a tool which can do it with a proper quality

comments.author: stuffedcrust_studios
comments.body: i guess what's weird is that the shoot animation has the wide leg stance, so every time she shoots the legs insta pop to a different position, looks especially bad when running and shooting. i think what a lot of these kinda games do is split the leg and top half into different sprites so they can animate independently maybe? so you can run and shoot at the same time.

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: That's a great suggestion, thanks! I'll probably try adjusting the shooting pose later, or maybe have the character stop moving while firing, which might make more sense.

comments.author: Bananaboy1107
comments.body:
Yeah, that's exactly the problem I ran into too. The animation part still takes way too much manual work.

That's actually why I've been experimenting with a tool that generates sprite animation frames directly from a character image. It's still early and not perfect, but I'm trying to reduce as much of the repetitive work as possible.

If you're curious, this is what I'm working on: https://www.bananagpt.ai/

I'd genuinely be interested to know whether something like this could fit into your workflow.

replies.author: Dependent-Video7534
replies.body: Thanks for sharing! I'll check it out when I get a chance.

comments.author: tabaxi_gf
comments.body: I would consider adding acceleration to the left/right movement.  This might add a little slide when stopping so you might want more animation frames for that (I suppose also you could have an acceleration to start but not to stop though that might also feel weird)  I think original Metal Slug does NOT have this though; because it's much lower pixel resolution I think the look is more acceptable for that game.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: I think the feedback of hitting those rectangles actually looks good! I hate to say this but I do think the player character looks a bit “ai-generic” I’d try to add some manual edits. You could also try to animate-interpolate feature with pixel lab to add some more frames to the animation to smooth it out a bit.

comments.author: manvsmidi
comments.body: Look up Disney's twelve basic principals of animation.  My professor shared them with me when I started doing 3D graphics.  Sometimes art just feels "off" and it's hard to say why.  If you go back to them, they really help as a guide.

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body: I think it looks great! Just needs a little polish here and there but other than that its looking awesome

comments.author: ekolimits
comments.body: You are missing the right camera work. Your camera can’t be stapled onto the character like that because it won’t feel fluid.

comments.author: Lavio00
comments.body: I feel like there need to be more animation frames inbetween each movement. Ie there are too few sprites in the sequence that make up the animations, if that makes sense?
